title: The Enneads, Vol. 1
author: Plotinus (MacKenna trans)
description: The Enneads, Volume 1, of Plotinus (c. 204-270 CE), in the translation by Stephen MacKenna (London: Medici Society, from 1917), the celebrated English rendering of the founder of Neoplatonism. The Enneads are fifty-four treatises arranged by Plotinus's disciple Porphyry into six groups of nine. MacKenna's first volume contains Porphyry's Life of Plotinus and the First Ennead, the ethical treatises on the living being and the human, the virtues, dialectic, happiness and whether it grows with time, beauty, the primal good and secondary goods, the nature and source of evil, and the 'reasoned dismissal' from life. Plotinus teaches the emanation of all reality from the One through Intellect (Nous) and Soul, and the soul's return to union with the One. MacKenna's lyrical translation, a lifelong labour, shaped the English reception of Neoplatonic mysticism.
